title: Prakrama 3, Sarga 10. Beholding Sri Purushottama
html:
Passing the Kapota-linga and the river Bhargavi, the Lord sees the temple of Jagannatha and falls senseless; above the temple a boy with a flute appears to Him; after bathing at the tirtha of Markandeya He enters the temple, and Jagannatha stretches out His hand to Him

Verse 1

पुनः शृणुष्व देवस्य चैतन्यस्य महात्मनः।
कथां मनोहरां पुण्यां नूतनामृतवर्षिणः॥१॥

punaḥ śṛṇuṣva devasya caitanyasya mahātmanaḥ|
kathāṁ manoharāṁ puṇyāṁ nūtanāmṛtavarṣiṇaḥ||1||

punah — again; shrinushva — hear; devasya — of the Lord; chaitanyasya — Chaitanya; maha-atmanah — the great soul; katham — the account; manoharam — heart-charming; punyam — holy; nutana-amrita-varshinah — who showers fresh nectar.

1Hear once more the holy, heart-charming account of the Lord Chaitanya, the great soul who showers fresh nectar.

Verse 2

ततः प्रयातो भगवान्मुदान्वितो
निजैरजः साधुजनैकबन्धुः।
कपोतसंपूजितलिङ्गमुत्तमं
दृष्ट्वा प्रणम्याशु पुनर्ययौ हरिः॥२॥

tataḥ prayāto bhagavānmudānvito
nijairajaḥ sādhujanaikabandhuḥ|
kapotasaṁpūjitaliṅgamuttamaṁ
dṛṣṭvā praṇamyāśu punaryayau hariḥ||2||

tatah — then; prayatah — setting out; bhagavan — Bhagavan; muda-anvitah — joyful; nijaih — with His own; ajah — the Unborn; sadhu-jana-eka-bandhuh — the one friend of the righteous; kapota-sampujita-lingam — the linga worshipped by a dove; uttamam — excellent; drishtva — seeing; pranamya — bowing; ashu — soon; punah — again; yayau — went on; harih — Hari.

2Then Bhagavan, the Unborn, the one friend of the righteous, set out joyfully with His companions; seeing the excellent linga worshipped by a dove1, Hari bowed and soon went on.

Verse 3

पुण्यान्शिवस्यान्यतमांश्च लिङ्गा-
न्विलोक्य हर्षेण नमन्पुनर्ययौ।
नदीं महावीर्यवतीं स भार्गवीं
तस्यां कृतस्नानविधिः पुनर्ययौ॥३॥

puṇyānśivasyānyatamāṁśca liṅgā-
nvilokya harṣeṇa namanpunaryayau|
nadīṁ mahāvīryavatīṁ sa bhārgavīṁ
tasyāṁ kṛtasnānavidhiḥ punaryayau||3||

punyan — holy; shivasya — of Shiva; anyataman — other; cha — and; lingan — lingas; vilokya — seeing; harshena — with joy; naman — bowing; punah — again; yayau — went on; nadim — the river; maha-viryavatim — mighty; sah — He; bhargavim — the Bhargavi; tasyam — in her; krita-snana-vidhih — having bathed according to rule; punah — again; yayau — went on.

3Seeing other holy lingas of Shiva as well, He bowed to them with joy and continued on His way; in the mighty river Bhargavi2 He bathed according to rule and went on again.

Verse 4

ततोऽवलोक्याशु हरेः सुमन्दिरं
सुधानुलिप्तं शरदिन्दुसुप्रभम्।
रथाङ्गयुक्तं पवनोद्धुतांशुकं
विभूषणं नीलगिरेर्महोज्ज्वलम्॥४॥

tato'valokyāśu hareḥ sumandiraṁ
sudhānuliptaṁ śaradindusuprabham|
rathāṅgayuktaṁ pavanoddhutāṁśukaṁ
vibhūṣaṇaṁ nīlagirermahojjvalam||4||

tatah — then; avalokya — beholding; ashu — soon; hareh — of Hari; su-mandiram — the beautiful temple; sudha-anuliptam — whitewashed; sharad-indu-su-prabham — shining like the autumn moon; rathanga-yuktam — crowned with the discus; pavana-uddhuta-amshukam — its cloth banners tossed by the wind; vibhushanam — the ornament; nila-gireh — of the Blue Mountain; maha-ujjvalam — brilliantly shining.

4Soon He beheld the beautiful temple of Hari: whitewashed, shining like the autumn moon, crowned with the discus, its banners tossed by the wind — the brilliant ornament of the Blue Mountain3.

Verse 5

कैलासशृङ्गं मुहुराक्षिपच्च
कान्त्या समुच्छेषतया सुधाम्ना।
प्रभञ्जनाकल्पितचेलहस्तै-
राहूयमानं कमलेक्षणं तम्॥५॥

kailāsaśṛṅgaṁ muhurākṣipacca
kāntyā samuccheṣatayā sudhāmnā|
prabhañjanākalpitacelahastai-
rāhūyamānaṁ kamalekṣaṇaṁ tam||5||

kailasa-shringam — the peak of Kailasa; muhuh — again and again; akshipat — putting to shame; cha — and; kantya — by its lustre; samuchchheshataya — by its height (?); su-dhamna — by its splendour; prabhanjana-akalpita-chela-hastaih — with hands of cloth set waving by the wind; ahuyamanam — being beckoned; kamala-ikshanam — the Lotus-eyed; tam — Him.

5With its lustre, its height4 and its splendour the temple put the peak of Kailasa to shame again and again, and with hands of cloth set waving by the wind it seemed to beckon the Lotus-eyed One.

Verse 6

पपात भूमौ सहसा हतारि-
र्हरिर्गतस्पन्दनमन्तरात्मा।
विलोक्य सर्वे मुमुहुस्तदीयाः
प्राणेन हीनास्तनवो यथार्याः॥६॥

papāta bhūmau sahasā hatāri-
rharirgataspandanamantarātmā|
vilokya sarve mumuhustadīyāḥ
prāṇena hīnāstanavo yathāryāḥ||6||

papata — fell; bhumau — to the ground; sahasa — suddenly; hata-arih — the Slayer of foes; harih — Hari; gata-spandanam — without motion; antar-atma — the inner Self; vilokya — seeing; sarve — all; mumuhuh — swooned; tadiyah — His companions; pranena — of the breath of life; hinah — bereft; tanavah — bodies; yatha — like; aryah — the noble ones.

6And suddenly Hari, the Slayer of foes, the inner Self of all, fell motionless to the ground. Seeing this, all His noble companions swooned, like bodies bereft of the breath of life.

Verse 7

ततः क्षणेनोत्थितमीशमुत्सुका
विलोक्य जीवं परिवव्रुरिन्द्रियाः।
तथैवमात्मानमतद्विदो जनाः
स्वभावतस्तान्भगवानथाब्रवीत्॥७॥

tataḥ kṣaṇenotthitamīśamutsukā
vilokya jīvaṁ parivavrurindriyāḥ|
tathaivamātmānamatadvido janāḥ
svabhāvatastānbhagavānathābravīt||7||

tatah — then; kshanena — after a moment; utthitam — risen; isham — the Lord; utsukah — anxious; vilokya — seeing; jivam — the life (soul); parivavruh — surrounded; indriyah — the senses; tatha — so; evam — thus; atmanam — His true Self; a-tat-vidah — not knowing that; janah — the people; svabhavatah — according to His nature; tan — to them; bhagavan — Bhagavan; atha — then; abravit — said.

7A moment later, seeing that the Lord had risen, they anxiously gathered round Him, as the senses gather round the life within. The people did not know His true nature5, and Bhagavan, as was His way, said to them:

Verse 8

भवन्त एवात्र हरेर्गृहोपरि
स्थितं महानीलमणिप्रभं प्रभुम्।
बालं प्रपश्यन्तु ततो न दृष्ट्वा
दृष्ट्वा तथोचुः प्रतिमां प्रभोर्द्विजाः॥८॥

bhavanta evātra harergṛhopari
sthitaṁ mahānīlamaṇiprabhaṁ prabhum|
bālaṁ prapaśyantu tato na dṛṣṭvā
dṛṣṭvā tathocuḥ pratimāṁ prabhordvijāḥ||8||

bhavantah — you; eva — yourselves; atra — here; hareh — of Hari; griha-upari — above the house; sthitam — standing; maha-nila-mani-prabham — shining like a great sapphire; prabhum — the Lord; balam — the boy; prapashyantu — may you see (behold); tatah — then; na — not; drishtva — seeing; drishtva — seeing; tatha — "so it is"; uchuh — said; pratimam — the image; prabhoh — of the Lord; dvijah — the brahmanas.

8"See for yourselves: there, above the house of Hari, stands the Lord — a boy shining like a great sapphire!" The brahmanas did not see the boy, but, looking at the Deity of the Lord, they answered, "Yes, we see."

Verse 9

मोहः पुनः स्यादिति शङ्क्यमान-
स्तानब्रवीत्पश्य हरेर्गृहध्वजम्।
आलक्ष्य बालं मुहुराक्षिपन्तं
वक्त्रेण पूर्णामृतरश्मिकोटिम्॥९॥

mohaḥ punaḥ syāditi śaṅkyamāna-
stānabravītpaśya harergṛhadhvajam|
ālakṣya bālaṁ muhurākṣipantaṁ
vaktreṇa pūrṇāmṛtaraśmikoṭim||9||

mohah — a swoon; punah — again; syat — may come; iti — that; shankyamanah — the one for whom it was feared; tan — to them; abravit — said; pashya — look; hareh — of Hari; griha-dhvajam — at the banner of the house; alakshya — making out; balam — the boy; muhuh — again and again; akshipantam — putting to shame; vaktrena — with His face; purna-amrita-rashmi-kotim — millions of full moons.

9Then He for whom they feared that He might swoon again said to them, "Look at the banner above the house of Hari: make out the boy whose face again and again puts to shame millions of full moons!

Verse 10

आलोलरक्ताङ्गुलिशोणपद्म-
तलेन मामाक्रमति स्म पाणिना।
दक्षेण सव्येन च वेणुरन्ध्र-
विन्यस्तवक्त्राङ्गुलिनातिशोभितः॥१०॥

ālolaraktāṅguliśoṇapadma-
talena māmākramati sma pāṇinā|
dakṣeṇa savyena ca veṇurandhra-
vinyastavaktrāṅgulinātiśobhitaḥ||10||

alola-rakta-anguli-shona-padma-talena — with its palm red as a lotus and its rosy fingers astir; mam — me; akramati sma — draws to Himself; panina — with His hand; dakshena — with the right; savyena — with the left; cha — and; venu-randhra-vinyasta-vaktra-angulina — with lips and fingers set to the holes of the flute; ati-shobhitah — exceedingly beautiful.

10With His hand — the red lotus of His palm, with its rosy fingers astir — He draws Me to Himself; and how beautiful He is as He puts His lips to the flute and sets the fingers of His right and left hands on its holes!

Verse 11

असौ सुधारश्मिसहस्रकान्तिः
को वा मनो मोहयति स्मितेन।
स एवमुत्कोऽतितरां जगाम
द्रुतं द्रुतस्वर्णरुचिः सभृत्यैः॥११॥

asau sudhāraśmisahasrakāntiḥ
ko vā mano mohayati smitena|
sa evamutko'titarāṁ jagāma
drutaṁ drutasvarṇaruciḥ sabhṛtyaiḥ||11||

asau — this one; sudha-rashmi-sahasra-kantih — with the radiance of a thousand moons; kah — who; va — then; manah — the mind; mohayati — enchants; smitena — with a smile; sah — He; evam — thus (saying); utkah — longing; ati-taram — exceedingly; jagama — went; drutam — swiftly; druta-svarna-ruchih — gleaming like molten gold; sa-bhrityaih — with His servants.

11Who is He, radiant as a thousand moons, whose smile enchants My mind?" Saying this, He who gleams like molten gold hastened on in utmost longing with His servants.

Verse 12

प्रासादमालोक्य जगत्पतेर्मुहु-
र्मुहुः स्खलन्नेत्रजवारिधारया।
शृङ्गः सुमेरोरिव निर्झरान्वित-
स्तीर्थं मृकण्डोरगमत्सुतस्य॥१२॥

prāsādamālokya jagatpatermuhu-
rmuhuḥ skhalannetrajavāridhārayā|
śṛṅgaḥ sumeroriva nirjharānvita-
stīrthaṁ mṛkaṇḍoragamatsutasya||12||

prasadam — the temple-palace; alokya — seeing; jagat-pateh — of the Lord of the world; muhuh muhuh — again and again; skhalan — stumbling; netra-ja-vari-dharaya — with streams of tears from His eyes; shringah — a peak; sumeroh — of Sumeru; iva — like; nirjhara-anvitah — with waterfalls; tirtham — to the tirtha; mrikandoh — of Mrikandu; agamat — came; sutasya — of the son.

12Gazing at the temple of the Lord of the world, He stumbled again and again; streams of tears poured from His eyes, and He was like a peak of Sumeru coursed by waterfalls. Thus He came to the tirtha of the son of Mrikandu6.

Verse 13

चक्रेण चक्रे स्वयमुग्रचक्रिणा
तीर्थं महेशाय सुदीप्तिमत्तटम्।
स्नात्वा च यस्मिन्शिवलोकमाप्ता-
स्तत्राशु गत्वा विधिवच्चकार॥१३॥

cakreṇa cakre svayamugracakriṇā
tīrthaṁ maheśāya sudīptimattaṭam|
snātvā ca yasminśivalokamāptā-
statrāśu gatvā vidhivaccakāra||13||

chakrena — with His discus; chakre — made; svayam — Himself; ugra-chakrina — by the fierce Bearer of the discus; tirtham — a tirtha; maheshaya — for Mahesha; su-dipti-mat-tatam — with gleaming banks; snatva — bathing; cha — and; yasmin — in which; shiva-lokam — the world of Shiva; aptah — have attained (men); tatra — there; ashu — quickly; gatva — going; vidhivat — according to rule; chakara — performed (the rites).

13This tirtha with its gleaming banks the fierce Bearer of the discus Himself made with His discus for Mahesha, and by bathing in it men have attained the world of Shiva. Hastening there, the Lord performed all that is prescribed.

Verse 14

स्नात्वा ततः शङ्करलिङ्गमीश्वरो
जपन्नघोरं प्रणनाम दण्डवत्।
स्तुत्वा महेशस्तुतिभिः सुमङ्गलै-
र्जगाम यज्ञेशमहालयं प्रभुः॥१४॥

snātvā tataḥ śaṅkaraliṅgamīśvaro
japannaghoraṁ praṇanāma daṇḍavat|
stutvā maheśastutibhiḥ sumaṅgalai-
rjagāma yajñeśamahālayaṁ prabhuḥ||14||

snatva — having bathed; tatah — then; shankara-lingam — to the linga of Shankara; ishvarah — the Lord; japan — murmuring; aghoram — the Aghora (mantra); prananama — bowed; dandavat — like a staff; stutva — having praised; mahesha-stutibhih — with hymns to Mahesha; su-mangalaih — most auspicious; jagama — went; yajna-isha-maha-alayam — to the great abode of the Lord of sacrifice; prabhuh — the Lord.

14Having bathed, the Lord murmured the Aghora mantra7 and bowed down like a staff to the linga of Shankara; and having praised Mahesha with most auspicious hymns, the Lord went to the great abode of the Lord of sacrifice8.

Verse 15

प्रहृष्टरोमा नयनाब्जवारिभिः
परीतवक्षाः परमात्मचिन्तया।
विवेश देवेशगृहं महोत्सवं
ननाम दृष्ट्वा जगतां पतिं प्रभुम्॥१५॥

prahṛṣṭaromā nayanābjavāribhiḥ
parītavakṣāḥ paramātmacintayā|
viveśa deveśagṛhaṁ mahotsavaṁ
nanāma dṛṣṭvā jagatāṁ patiṁ prabhum||15||

prahrishta-roma — His hair standing on end; nayana-abja-varibhih — with the waters of His lotus eyes; parita-vakshah — His chest bathed; parama-atma-chintaya — through meditation on the Supreme Self; vivesha — entered; deva-isha-griham — the house of the Lord of the gods; maha-utsavam — full of great festivity; nanama — bowed; drishtva — seeing; jagatam — of the worlds; patim — the Lord; prabhum — the Master.

15The hair of His body stood on end, His chest was bathed in the waters of His lotus eyes, His mind was absorbed in the Supreme Self; thus He entered the festive house of the Lord of the gods and, seeing the Master of the worlds, bowed down.

Verse 16

पपात भूमौ पुनरेव दण्डव-
न्नमन्मुहुः प्रेमभराकुलाननः।
ततः क्षणान्मुष्टिकरं विभावय-
ञ्जगत्पतिं सोऽतिरुरोद विह्वलः॥१६॥

papāta bhūmau punareva daṇḍava-
nnamanmuhuḥ premabharākulānanaḥ|
tataḥ kṣaṇānmuṣṭikaraṁ vibhāvaya-
ñjagatpatiṁ so'tiruroda vihvalaḥ||16||

papata — fell; bhumau — to the ground; punah — again; eva — indeed; dandavat — like a staff; naman — bowing; muhuh — again and again; prema-bhara-akula-ananah — His face distraught with the weight of love; tatah — then; kshanat — after a moment; mushti-karam — with hands like fists; vibhavayan — perceiving; jagat-patim — the Lord of the world; sah — He; ati-ruroda — wept bitterly; vihvalah — overwhelmed.

16Again He fell to the ground like a staff, bowing again and again, His face distraught with the weight of love. And after a moment, perceiving that the hands of the Lord of the world were like clenched fists9, He was overwhelmed and wept bitterly.

Verse 17

दृष्ट्वा तमित्थं पुरुषोत्तमो हरिः
प्रसार्य पाणिं कमलाङ्ककोमलम्।
अदर्शयद्रक्ततलं ततो मुदा
चैतन्यदेवो हृषितो जहास॥१७॥

dṛṣṭvā tamitthaṁ puruṣottamo hariḥ
prasārya pāṇiṁ kamalāṅkakomalam|
adarśayadraktatalaṁ tato mudā
caitanyadevo hṛṣito jahāsa||17||

drishtva — seeing; tam — Him; ittham — thus; purushottamah — Purushottama; harih — Hari; prasarya — stretching out; panim — His hand; kamala-anka-komalam — soft and marked with the lotus; adarshayat — showed; rakta-talam — with its red palm; tatah — then; muda — with joy; chaitanya-devah — Chaitanyadeva; hrishitah — delighted; jahasa — laughed.

17Seeing Him thus, Hari Purushottama stretched out to Him His soft hand marked with the lotus and showed Him its red palm; and Chaitanyadeva, delighted, laughed for joy.

Verse 18

उवाच चैवं करुणाम्बुधे त्वं
प्रसीद देवेश महेशवन्दित।
पुनर्न दृष्ट्वा करपल्लवाङ्गुलिं
रुरोद तस्मिन्द्विगुणं स विह्वलः॥१८॥

uvāca caivaṁ karuṇāmbudhe tvaṁ
prasīda deveśa maheśavandita|
punarna dṛṣṭvā karapallavāṅguliṁ
ruroda tasmindviguṇaṁ sa vihvalaḥ||18||

uvacha — said; cha — and; evam — thus; karuna-ambudhe — O ocean of mercy; tvam — You; prasida — be gracious; deva-isha — O Lord of the gods; mahesha-vandita — worshipped by Mahesha; punah — again; na — not; drishtva — seeing; kara-pallava-angulim — the fingers of the bud-like hand; ruroda — wept; tasmin — then; dvi-gunam — twice as much; sah — He; vihvalah — overwhelmed.

18And He said, "O ocean of mercy, be gracious, Lord of the gods, worshipped by Mahesha!" But no longer seeing the fingers of that hand, tender as a young shoot, He was overwhelmed and wept twice as much.

Verse 19

पुनश्च दृष्ट्वातिमहोत्सवान्वितो
हर्षाश्रुधाराप्लुतदेहयष्टिः॥१९॥

punaśca dṛṣṭvātimahotsavānvito
harṣāśrudhārāplutadehayaṣṭiḥ||19||

punah — again; cha — and; drishtva — seeing; ati-maha-utsava-anvitah — filled with the greatest jubilation; harsha-ashru-dhara-apluta-deha-yashtih — His slender body drenched with streams of tears of joy.

19And seeing them again, He was filled with the greatest jubilation, and His slender body was drenched with streams of tears of joy10.

Verse 20

एवं तयोरुद्भटचेष्टितं जनाः
शृण्वन्ति गायन्ति परं व्रजन्ति ते।
पदं मुरारेः परमार्थदर्शिनो
न यत्र भूयः पतनं क्वचिद्भवेत्॥२०॥

evaṁ tayorudbhaṭaceṣṭitaṁ janāḥ
śṛṇvanti gāyanti paraṁ vrajanti te|
padaṁ murāreḥ paramārthadarśino
na yatra bhūyaḥ patanaṁ kvacidbhavet||20||

evam — thus; tayoh — of the two; udbhata-cheshtitam — the wondrous doings; janah — people; shrinvanti — hear; gayanti — sing; param — the supreme; vrajanti — reach; te — they; padam — abode; murareh — of Murari; parama-artha-darshinah — seeing the highest truth; na — not; yatra — where; bhuyah — again; patanam — fall; kvachit — ever; bhavet — there is.

20People who hear and sing of these wondrous doings of the two of Them come to see the highest truth and reach the supreme abode of Murari, from which there is never again a fall.

Thus ends the tenth sarga, "Beholding Sri Purushottama" (Shri-purushottama-darshana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The Kapota-linga ("the linga of the dove"), a shrine of Shiva on the way from Bhubaneshvara to Puri.
  2. The Bhargavi is a river in Orissa flowing near Puri.
  3. The Blue Mountain is Nilachala (Nilagiri), the hill on which the temple of Jagannatha stands at Purushottama (Puri).
  4. The rendering of this word is conjectural.
  5. The second half of the verse is obscure; the rendering is conjectural.
  6. The son of Mrikandu is the sage Markandeya; his tirtha (the Markandeya pond) is at Puri.
  7. Aghora: one of the mantras of Shiva (named after one of his faces).
  8. That is, of Jagannatha.
  9. The Deity of Jagannatha has rounded arms without hands; the Lord grieves at not seeing His palms, and Jagannatha in His mercy shows Him His hand (vv. 17–18).
  10. In all the editions only half of this verse survives.
